answer: Forced-divergence challenge routing: each identity gets a hidden seed at its vertex in a routing graph, and verifiers route probe queries along seed-dependent paths that a copy must reproduce. Clones pass only if they answer every path identically, so the attacker must either run one shared state per copy—exposing a whisper of divergence under concurrent multi-path probes—or fork the seed, which a prism of cross-path consistency checks catches. Each forced fork costs a full independent state rebuild plus lost shared context, charged per identity per epoch.
